drivingQuestion: Why state that the fallen are buried where they fell?

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא אוֹמֵר: אַף חוֹנִין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁנֶּהֱרָגִים שָׁם נִקְבָּרִים. פְּשִׁיטָא, מֵת מִצְוָה הוּא, וּמֵת מִצְוָה קוֹנֶה מְקוֹמוֹ!
segments.en: It was taught in the Tosefta that «Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says: They may also encamp in any place, and in the place where they were killed, there they are buried.» The Gemara raises a difficulty: This is «obvious,» as a body of a dead soldier «is» considered to be «a corpse with no one to bury it [met mitzva],» and the principle is that «a met mitzva acquires its place.» In other words, the body must be interred where it is found, and the owner of the field cannot prevent burial.

moves.summary: obvious: met mitzva acquires its place
moves.about: burial where killed is obvious since a met mitzva acquires its place
